introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.content: Your privacy is our absolute priority. Pacifinance has been designed from the ground up with privacy at its core. This policy explains how we handle your data with maximum respect for your privacy.

dataCollection.title: Data Collection
dataCollection.content: We only collect data essential for the service to function:
items: Financial and profile data voluntarily entered to provide the service

dataUsage.title: Data Usage
dataUsage.content: Your data is used exclusively to provide platform functionality. We do not sell financial data or use it for advertising or commercial profiling.

benchmarkParticipation.title: Community benchmarks
benchmarkParticipation.content: Participation in hosted benchmarks is optional and requires separate consent in your profile. When enabled, we use only aggregated metrics and profile buckets to calculate group statistics subject to minimum privacy thresholds; transactions, notes and the public identifier are not shared. You can revoke consent at any time: stored benchmark profile buckets are deleted.

anonymity.title: Anonymity
anonymity.content: Statistics shown to participants are aggregated and never expose transactions, notes or identity. Your account data remains pseudonymous within the infrastructure needed to provide the service.

contact.title: Contact
contact.content: For any questions regarding this privacy policy, contact us through the platform's official channels.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions

questions.question: Is Pacifinance really free?
questions.answer: Yes, Pacifinance is completely free. There are no hidden costs, subscriptions, or limitations. The platform is supported by voluntary donations.

questions.question: How does privacy work on Pacifinance?
questions.answer: Privacy is at the heart of everything we do. Your data is always anonymous and never shared. We only use technical cookies necessary for operation.

questions.question: How can I compare myself with other users?
questions.answer: Comparisons are completely anonymous and based on aggregated data. You can see general statistics by category, sector, or geographic area without ever revealing your identity.

questions.question: What type of data can I enter?
questions.answer: You can enter income, outflows, investments, savings, and other financial data. All data remains anonymous and is used only for your personal analysis.

questions.question: How can I support the project?
questions.answer: The best way to support Pacifinance is through voluntary donations via Buy Me a Coffee. Every contribution helps us keep the platform online and develop new features.

faq.contactInfo: Contact us through our official channels for assistance.

knowledge.title: Financial Knowledge
knowledge.subtitle: Learn to better manage your personal finances with practical guides and expert tips
knowledge.disclaimer: ⚠️ The information provided is for educational purposes and does not constitute personalized financial advice. Always consult a qualified financial advisor for important decisions.

content.intro: Investing means putting your money into financial instruments with the goal of obtaining a return over time. It's essential to diversify your portfolio, understand the risks associated with each instrument, and have a clear time horizon. Remember: time is your best ally in investing.

etf.title: ETF (Exchange Traded Fund)
etf.description: ETFs are funds that replicate an index (e.g., S&P 500, MSCI World, FTSE 100) and can be bought/sold on the stock exchange like stocks. They allow diversification with small amounts and are ideal for beginners. There are equity, bond, sector, and thematic ETFs. Management costs (TER) are typically between 0.05% and 0.50% annually.
etf.pros:
• Automatic diversification across hundreds of securities
• Very low management costs (TER 0.05%-0.50%)
• High liquidity - sellable anytime
• Full transparency on composition
• Ideal for DCA (Dollar Cost Averaging)
• No active management required
etf.cons:
• Follow the market even in downturns
• Never beat the reference index
• Currency risk for foreign ETFs
• Bid-ask spread on less liquid ETFs

stocks.title: Stocks
stocks.description: Stocks represent ownership shares in a company. Their value depends on company performance, market sentiment, and macroeconomic conditions. Investing in individual stocks requires time for fundamental and technical analysis. Recommended only after gaining experience with simpler instruments.
stocks.pros:
• Potential high returns (historically 7-10% annually)
• Periodic dividends from mature companies
• Voting rights in shareholder meetings
• Possibility to beat the market with good picks
• Immediate liquidity on major markets
stocks.cons:
• High risk of capital loss
• Requires time for analysis and monitoring
• High short-term volatility
• Concentration risk with few stocks
• Emotional biases can lead to bad decisions

bonds.title: Bonds
bonds.description: Bonds are loans you make to entities (states, companies). In return, you receive periodic interest (coupons) and capital at maturity. Risk varies: government bonds from stable countries are safe, corporate or high-yield bonds are riskier but with higher returns. Bond prices move inversely to interest rates.
bonds.pros:
• More predictable returns than stocks
• Periodic coupons as cash flow
• Generally lower risk
• Excellent diversification from stock market
• Capital protection at maturity
bonds.cons:
• Historically lower returns than stocks
• Inflation risk erodes real value
• Interest rate risk: if rates rise, prices fall
• Default risk for less solid issuers
• Lower liquidity for corporate bonds

crypto.title: Cryptocurrencies
crypto.description: Decentralized digital currencies based on blockchain technology. Bitcoin is the most known and 'stable', Ethereum is second by market cap. There are thousands of altcoins with different characteristics. It's a highly speculative market, open 24/7, with little regulation. Recommended only for a small portfolio percentage (max 5-10%).
crypto.pros:
• Potential very high returns
• Decentralization and independence from banks
• Continuous technological innovation
• Market open 24/7
• Staking possibilities for passive income
• Global accessibility without intermediaries
crypto.cons:
• Extreme volatility (20-50% swings common)
• Uncertain and variable regulation
• Technological and hacking risk
• No protection in case of loss
• Difficult fundamental valuation
• Risk of fraudulent projects (scams)

government_bonds.title: Government Bonds
government_bonds.description: Bonds issued by the state to finance public debt. In the US: Treasury Bonds/Bills. In UK: Gilts. In Germany: Bunds. They're among the safest investments if issued by stable countries, guaranteed by the state's taxation ability.
government_bonds.pros:
• High security (minimal default risk)
• Government guarantee
• Fixed and predictable return
• Tax advantages in some countries
• High liquidity on secondary markets
• Capital protection at maturity
government_bonds.cons:
• Generally low returns
• Inflation risk during high inflation periods
• Country risk for less stable states
• Interest rate risk
• Sometimes negative real returns

real_estate.title: Real Estate & REITs
real_estate.description: Real estate investment can be direct (buying property) or indirect through REITs (Real Estate Investment Trusts) and real estate funds. REITs allow investing in real estate with small amounts and high liquidity, diversifying across many properties.
real_estate.pros:
• Tangible and understandable asset
• Long-term inflation protection
• Income from rent or REIT dividends
• Diversification from stock market
• REITs offer liquidity and accessibility
real_estate.cons:
• Direct property requires high capital
• Maintenance and management costs
• Low liquidity for direct property
• Geographic concentration risk
• Interest rate sensitivity

beginner_tips.title: Tips for Beginners
tips: Start with diversified ETFs on global indices (e.g., MSCI World, S&P 500)
Never invest money you need in the next 3-5 years
Use DCA (Dollar Cost Averaging): invest the same amount every month
Don't try to 'beat the market' - even professionals struggle
Study at least 6 months before buying individual stocks
Keep maximum 5-10% of portfolio in cryptocurrencies
Always diversify: never more than 5% on a single stock
Ignore daily news - think long-term (10+ years)
Reinvest dividends to leverage compound interest
Have an emergency fund BEFORE starting to invest

saving.title: Saving
saving.subtitle: How to build your financial foundation

content.intro: Saving is the foundation of financial health. Before investing, it's essential to have an emergency fund and clear goals. People who actively save typically achieve their financial goals 3x faster than those who don't.

emergency_fund.title: Emergency Fund
emergency_fund.description: An emergency fund should cover 3-6 months of expenses. Keep it in high-yield savings accounts or easily accessible accounts. This protects you from unexpected events like job loss, medical emergencies, or major repairs.
tips: Calculate your essential monthly expenses (not income)
Multiply by 3 months (minimum) to 6 months (ideal)
Keep this money in safe and liquid accounts
Don't touch except for real emergencies (not 'wants')
Review the fund annually based on life changes

savings_goals.title: Savings Goals
savings_goals.description: Having clear and quantifiable goals helps stay motivated. Use the SMART method: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound. Distinguish between short, medium, and long-term goals.
savings_goals.short_term: Short term (1-2 years): Vacation ($1,000-3,000), appliances, training course, emergency fund
savings_goals.medium_term: Medium term (2-5 years): Car ($10,000-30,000), wedding, home renovation, mortgage down payment
savings_goals.long_term: Long term (5+ years): House, retirement, children's education, financial independence

saving_strategies.title: Saving Strategies
strategies: Pay yourself first: set up automatic transfer on payday
Automate savings to separate accounts for different goals
Track ALL expenses for at least 1 month - you'll be surprised
Compare prices and use cashback for important purchases
Apply the 24-48 hour rule for impulse purchases

high_yield_savings.title: Savings and Deposit Accounts
high_yield_savings.description: High-yield savings accounts offer returns above standard checking accounts. Compare offers from online banks that often offer better rates. Distinguish between fixed-term deposits (higher rates but locked funds) and instant access accounts (lower return but immediate access).
tips: Compare rates on comparison websites
Consider online banks for better rates (up to 3-5% for fixed term)
Verify FDIC/FSCS insurance coverage ($250,000/£85,000 per bank)
Use instant access for emergency fund, fixed term for goal-dated savings
Watch out for promotional rates - read the fine print

budgeting.title: Budget Management
budgeting.subtitle: How to plan and control your expenses

content.intro: A budget helps you control where your money goes and reach your financial goals. It shouldn't be rigid, but a flexible guide that adapts to your life. People who keep a budget save on average 20% more than those who don't.

budget_creation.title: How to Create an Effective Budget
steps: Calculate your monthly net income (salary + other income)
List all fixed expenses: rent/mortgage, utilities, insurance, subscriptions
Analyze 3 months of bank statements for real variable expenses
Categorize: food, transport, entertainment, shopping, health, other
Assign a realistic percentage to savings (start with 10%)
Review the budget every month and adjust categories
Celebrate small wins to maintain motivation

methods.50_30_20: 50/30/20: 50% essential needs (rent, food, utilities), 30% wants (entertainment, hobbies), 20% savings and investments. Simple and flexible.
methods.envelope: Envelope method: Withdraw cash and divide into envelopes by category. When the envelope is empty, stop spending. Great for controlling impulse spending.
methods.zero_based: Zero-based budget: Every dollar must have an assigned purpose. Income - Expenses = 0. Requires more time but maximum control.
methods.pay_yourself_first: Pay yourself first: Automate savings on payday, then live with the rest. Simple and effective.
methods.kakeibo: Kakeibo (Japanese): Record every expense by hand, reflect on each purchase asking 'Do I really need this?'. Increases awareness.

outflow_tracking.title: Smart Outflow Tracking
tips: Use Pacifinance for a unified view of all accounts
Categorize expenses immediately - don't procrastinate
Check your account at least 2 times per week
Identify 'phantom expenses': small purchases that add up
Analyze patterns: when do you spend more? (weekends, evenings, stress)
Compare month over month to see progress
Set alerts for categories at risk of overspending

reduce_expenses.title: How to Reduce Expenses Without Suffering
tips: Renegotiate contracts: phone, internet, insurance (10-30% savings)
Cook at home 2-3 more times per week (save $100-200/month)
Use the library instead of buying books
Share streaming subscriptions with family/friends
Buy used for electronics, clothes, furniture
Use public transport or bike when possible
Plan meals weekly to avoid waste
Bring lunch to work 3+ times per week

salary_management.title: Salary Management
salary_management.subtitle: How to optimize your income and make it grow

content.intro: Salary management isn't just about how to spend it, but also how to optimize, protect, and grow it over time. A strategic approach can make the difference between living paycheck to paycheck and building wealth.

breakdown.needs: Essential Needs (50-60%): Rent/mortgage, utilities, groceries, necessary transport, mandatory insurance. If you exceed 60%, look to reduce or increase income.
breakdown.wants: Wants (20-30%): Restaurants, streaming, hobbies, non-essential shopping, gym, travel. This is the most flexible category.
breakdown.savings: Savings and Investments (20%+): Emergency fund (priority 1), long-term investments, pension. The goal is to reach 30% over time.

tax_optimization.title: Legal Tax Optimization
tips: Maximize 401(k)/pension contributions for tax-deferred growth
Use HSA/FSA for medical expenses (triple tax advantage)
Consider Roth IRA for tax-free retirement income
Track deductible expenses: student loan interest, home office
Harvest tax losses to offset capital gains
Use company benefits: 401k matching is free money
Meal vouchers are often tax-exempt (up to $8/day for electronic ones)
Consult a tax professional for complex situations

income_growth.title: Growing Your Income
strategies: Update skills: online courses, industry certifications
Negotiate salary: prepare market data, document achievements
Change companies every 2-4 years: often the only way for significant salary jumps
Side hustle: content creation, consulting, online selling
Invest in yourself: foreign languages, soft skills, networking
Passive income: dividends, rentals, royalties (requires initial capital)

first_salary.title: First Salary: How to Start Right
tips: Don't inflate your lifestyle immediately - live like a student for 1-2 years
Set up automatic savings transfer immediately (at least 10%)
Build emergency fund first (3 months of expenses)
Don't buy a new car - it's the worst financial decision
Start investing even $50-100/month - time is on your side
Avoid consumer debt (financing, revolving credit cards)
Take advantage of company 401k matching if available

portfolio_management.title: Portfolio Management
portfolio_management.subtitle: How to balance and optimize your investments

content.intro: A diversified portfolio reduces risks and optimizes long-term returns. The key is strategic allocation between different investment classes, based on your time horizon and risk tolerance. There's no perfect portfolio for everyone.

asset_allocation.title: Asset Allocation by Profile
asset_allocation.description: Distribute your investments among different categories based on your age, goals, and risk tolerance. A simple rule: 100 minus your age = % in stocks.
asset_allocation.conservative: Conservative (near retirement, low risk tolerance): 70-80% bonds/cash, 20-30% stocks. Priority: capital preservation.
asset_allocation.moderate: Moderate (30-50 years, medium tolerance): 50-60% stocks, 30-40% bonds, 10% alternatives. Growth/safety balance.
asset_allocation.aggressive: Aggressive (young, high tolerance, long horizon): 80-90% stocks, 10-15% bonds, 5% alternatives. Maximize growth, accept volatility.

diversification.title: Diversification Principles
principles: Never more than 5-10% on a single stock - even the best companies can fail
Diversify by geographic area: 40-50% US, 20-30% Europe, 10-20% Emerging, 10% home country
Diversify by sector: technology, healthcare, finance, energy, consumer - avoid concentration
Diversify by size: large cap (stability), mid cap, small cap (growth)
Multi-asset: stocks, bonds, real estate (REITs), commodities, gold
Diversify over time: monthly DCA instead of lump sum (dollar cost averaging)
Decorrelation: assets that move differently (stocks vs gold)

rebalancing.title: Portfolio Rebalancing
rebalancing.description: Over time, some assets grow more than others, unbalancing the portfolio. Rebalancing brings proportions back to target, selling what grew and buying what declined.
rebalancing.frequency: Check every 6 months, rebalance 1-2 times per year maximum
rebalancing.trigger: Rebalance when a category deviates >5-10% from target
rebalancing.method: Method 1: Sell grown assets, buy fallen ones. Method 2: Direct new contributions toward underweight categories.

common_mistakes.title: Common Mistakes to Avoid
tips: Panic selling during crashes - historically always recovered
Buying after big rallies due to FOMO (Fear Of Missing Out)
Checking portfolio every day - creates unnecessary anxiety
Trying to time the market - almost impossible
Concentrating everything in home country stocks (home bias)
Ignoring costs: TER, commissions, spreads erode returns
Following 'gurus' advice on social media
Not having a written plan - leads to emotional decisions

general_knowledge.title: Fundamental Concepts
general_knowledge.subtitle: The basics of personal finance everyone should know

compound_interest.title: Compound Interest - The Eighth Wonder
compound_interest.description: Compound interest is the most powerful concept in finance. It means earning interest not only on initial capital, but also on already accrued interest. Einstein called it 'the eighth wonder of the world'. The earlier you start, the more time it has to work.

risk_return.title: Risk-Return Relationship
risk_return.description: Fundamental rule: the higher the potential return, the higher the risk. There are no high returns without risk - if someone promises you that, it's a scam. It's crucial to understand your risk profile and sleep peacefully at night.
risk_levels: Low risk: Savings accounts, T-Bills, short-term bonds (1-3% annual). Capital practically guaranteed.
Medium risk: Diversified equity ETFs, balanced funds (5-8% historical annual). Possible 20-30% drops.
High risk: Individual stocks, cryptocurrencies, derivatives. Possible 100%+ gains but also 50%+ losses.

inflation.title: Inflation - The Silent Enemy
inflation.description: Inflation erodes the purchasing power of money over time. $1,000 today will buy less in 10 years. With average 2% inflation, in 20 years your money loses about 33% of real value. This is why you shouldn't hold too much cash.
inflation.protection: Protect savings by investing in assets that historically beat inflation: stocks (7-10% historical), real estate, TIPS/inflation-linked bonds. Keep in cash only emergency fund and expenses planned within 1-2 years.

financial_independence.title: Financial Independence (FIRE)
financial_independence.description: The ultimate goal for many: having enough investments to live off returns without having to work. The FIRE movement (Financial Independence, Retire Early) popularized this concept. Requires a high savings rate (40-70%) for many years.
financial_independence.rule_25: Rule of 25: Accumulate 25 times your annual expenses in investments. If you spend $30,000/year, you need $750,000.
financial_independence.withdrawal_rate: 4% Rule: Withdraw maximum 4% annually from portfolio to maintain it over time (based on Trinity Study). Some suggest 3.5% for greater safety.

debt_management.title: Debt Management
debt_management.description: Not all debt is equal. 'Good' debt (mortgage, student loans) can be strategic. 'Bad' debt (credit cards, high-rate consumer loans) should be eliminated as a priority.
tips: Priority 1: Eliminate high-interest debt (>10%) before investing
Avalanche method: pay off highest interest rate debt first
Snowball method: pay off smallest debt first (psychological wins)
Never finance depreciating assets (cars, electronics, clothes)
Mortgage: consider as rent + forced investment, not 'bad debt'

financial_scams.title: How to Recognize Financial Scams
tips: Guaranteed high returns = SCAM (no one can guarantee returns)
Pressure to decide now = red flag
'Exclusive opportunity' = almost always Ponzi scheme
I don't understand how it works = don't invest
Promises to double money quickly = scam
Always verify: SEC for US, FCA for UK, relevant authority for your country
If it seems too good to be true, it is

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.question1: How can I add an income or an outflow?
faq.answer1: To add an income or an outflow, go to the 'Insert data' section and select the type of entry you want to make. Fill in the required fields and confirm the entry.
faq.question2: How can I update my balance?
faq.answer2: To update your balance, go to the 'Insert data' section and select the 'Update Balance' section. Fill in the required fields and confirm the update.
faq.question3: How can I delete an income or an outflow?
faq.answer3: To delete an income or an outflow, go to the 'Insert data' section and select the 'Add Incomes' or 'Add Outflows' section. In the table of incomes or outflows, select the income or outflow you want to delete and click on 'Delete'.
faq.question4: How can I change my id?
faq.answer4: To change your id, go to the 'Your Profile' section and select the 'Change ID' section. Fill in the required fields and confirm the id change.
faq.question5: How can I change my password?
faq.answer5: To change your password, go to the 'Your Profile' section and select the 'Change password' section. Fill in the required fields and confirm the password change.
faq.question6: How can I support the project?
faq.answer6: The project is non-profit and is supported by voluntary donations. If you think the service offered is useful and want to contribute, you can leave feedback and/or support us through a donation.
faq.answer6CallToAction: On every page at the bottom right you will find a pop-up to support the project. Thanks from the whole team!.
faq.question7: How can I delete my account?
faq.answer7: To delete your account, go to the 'Your Profile' section and select the 'Delete account' section. Confirm the deletion and you're done.
faq.question8: Can I install Pacifinance as an app?
faq.answer8: Yes! Pacifinance is a Progressive Web App (PWA) and can be installed on any device — iPhone, Android or desktop — directly from your browser. Go to Settings for step-by-step instructions for your device.

pwaInstall.title: Install as App
pwaInstall.subtitle: Use Pacifinance like a native app
pwaInstall.intro: Pacifinance can be installed as an app on your device for quick access, offline support, and a native-like experience — no app store needed.
pwaInstall.tip: Once installed, Pacifinance will appear on your home screen like any other app, with a faster loading time and full-screen experience.

ios: Open Pacifinance in Safari (required — it doesn't work from Chrome or other browsers on iOS)
Tap the Share button (the square with the upward arrow) at the bottom of the screen
Scroll down and tap "Add to Home Screen"
Give it a name (or leave Pacifinance) and tap "Add"
Done! You'll find Pacifinance on your home screen
android: Open Pacifinance in Chrome (or another supported browser)
Tap the three-dot menu (⋮) in the top-right corner
Tap "Add to Home screen" or "Install app"
Confirm by tapping "Install" in the popup
Done! Pacifinance is now installed and available from your home screen
desktop: Open Pacifinance in Chrome, Edge, or another Chromium-based browser
Click the install icon (⊕) in the address bar, or open the browser menu (⋮) and select "Install Pacifinance"
Confirm by clicking "Install" in the dialog
Done! Pacifinance will open in its own window and appear in your app launcher
